name: Bucket hat

card.summary: A soft, brimmed casual hat that adds a streetwear or retro look and shades the face and scalp from the sun.
card.aka: Irish walking hat, session hat, piluso (Argentina)

quick.overview:
The bucket hat is a soft hat with a downward-sloping brim all the way round. It began as a wool or tweed hat for rain in Ireland, was later issued in cotton to US troops, and became a street-fashion staple through hip-hop and later catwalk revivals.
For looks it works as a styling piece: it changes the silhouette of the head, can cover a hairline or hairstyle, and gives casual outfits a streetwear feel. Its brim also shades the face and scalp.
quick.how: People wear it with casual outfits, festival clothing and outdoor wear. Materials range from cotton and nylon to wool. Wearers choose a size that sits at the forehead and decide whether to wear the brim down or flipped up.
quick.risks: It carries no medical risks. Wearing hats in general can compress hair and some people note hat-hair; the brim offers shade but is not a substitute for sunscreen.

lead: A bucket hat is a casual, brimmed hat made of soft fabric. It is said to date from around 1900, when Irish farmers and fishermen wore wool felt or tweed versions against rain; the natural lanolin in raw wool helped repel water [1].

The modern form descends from a lightweight olive-drab cotton hat issued to the US Army during the Vietnam War; civilians adopted it for fishing and sun protection [1]. Mods wore it in the 1960s, and rappers including LL Cool J and Run-DMC made it a hip-hop fashion item in the 1980s and 1990s [1].

It returned to catwalks in the 2010s after celebrities such as Rihanna wore it, and luxury houses including Gucci, Loewe and Prada have made versions [1]. As a style item it adds a streetwear or retro look and provides sun shade for the face.

paras: After the interwar years the Irish walking hat spread internationally because it folded into a coat pocket, could be sponged clean and could be reshaped with kettle steam [1]. The cotton military version later reached civilians, and in the 1960s Mod subculture members wore it and it was adapted into women's fashion [1].
In Argentina the hat is called the piluso and is tied to football supporter culture; its popularity there reportedly rose after the 2022 World Cup [1].

The bucket hat is typically worn for its casual look and for shade; Wikipedia lists festival wear, fishing and sun protection among its uses [1]. Online style discussion treats it as an easy way to add a retro or streetwear element.
